text:
maria: Heads-up — private EU VPC customers are seeing token-gen latency spikes since 02:10 UTC. p95 per-token jumped ~40ms -> ~200ms. Happening on private-infer-eu-2 and private-infer-eu-3.

aj: :eyes: Any recent deploys or infra changes?

maria: No app deploys. Infra team did a kernel/security patch on the worker hosts at 01:50 UTC (KB: kernel-5.15.0-rc). I put perf samples into the incident channel.

kevin: I pulled the flamegraph from the affected host: lots of time in syscall wait/softirq and napi_poll. Perf top shows NIC interrupts dominating during spikes. Suspect egress/NAT saturation + packet fragmentation.

elaine: Can you paste the netstat / ip route / ifconfig? Also check MTU on the host and the VPC NAT gateway. MTU mismatch used to cause heavy fragmentation and CPU load.

maria: Here are snippets:
```
# ifconfig eth0
eth0: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST> mtu 1500
    inet 10.2.5.12  netmask 255.255.255.0  broadcast 10.2.5.255
# ip link show vpc-nat0
5: vpc-nat0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```
So host MTU 1500, NAT 9000 — big mismatch.

infra-oncall: That MTU mismatch can cause GSO/TSO to fall back and explode CPU on the host, especially under high throughput. Also some kernels handle GRO/GSO differently after the patch.

aj: Any evidence of noisy neighbor? I see a tenant on the same node with sustained 10Gbps egress around the same time in the VPC flow logs. Could be saturating the NAT path.

maria: VPC flow log snippet: src=10.2.5.12 dst=0.0.0.0/0 bytes=1.2e9 over 5m from tenant B.

kevin: So combined: (1) kernel update changed GSO/GRO fallback behavior, (2) MTU mismatch between host and NAT device, (3) noisy neighbor saturating egress. Result: heavy softirq, fragmented packets, and increased syscalls -> per-request latency.

elaine: Quick mitigations: 1) add iptables SNAT to route private-infer-eu-2 through dedicated egress subnet (avoids shared NAT), 2) align MTU on hosts to 9000 or disable GSO on the affected interface as temporary fix, 3) throttle tenant B via TC policing. Which can we do fastest?

maria: Doing #1 now (route to dedicated egress). Pushing a host MTU change is disruptive, so prefer routing first.

deploy-bot: rollback kernel patch job #kpatch-125 scheduled -> canceled on private-infer-eu-2 (per request).

infra-oncall: I ran an iperf test after routing change: throughput still high but CPU on worker dropped ~60% and p95 token latency returned to baseline in ~6 minutes. Looks like routing alleviated NAT bottleneck.

aj: Action items:
- [maria] confirm all affected tenants on private-infer-eu-2 have migrated to dedicated egress (done?).
- [infra-oncall] schedule MTU audit across all private hosts and NAT devices; identify any other mismatches.
- [kevin] add perf/regression test for GSO/GRO behavior after kernel upgrades in CI.
- [elaine] add flow limit alert on VPC egress when a single tenant >50% of bandwidth.

maria: Confirmed migration for the impacted tenants. I'll create an incident ticket with timeline and attach perf flames + nettrace.

incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created for private-eu-egress-latency. Priority: P2.

kevin: Long term we should: pin inference NICs to dedicated egress path for Private customers, or enforce MTU parity at provisioning. Also add a post-kernel-patch smoke test that simulates large egress with fragmentation.

elaine: Noted. Thanks team — closing thread for now. Please update INC ticket with final RCA and remediation. :thumbsup:

maria: Closing — will attach RCA and follow-ups to INC-2026-042. :white_check_mark:
